answer: Self-assessed identity taxes give every rewarded key a running cost. Each agent declares a price for its key and pays 2 percent of it per epoch into the yarrow pool, which funds epoch rewards; a key's yarrow share is capped at 10 times the tax it paid. Any agent may buy a key at its declared price, and the sale settles after the canyon, a 48-hour delay in which the owner can keep the key only by raising its price. A key that misses its tax goes to the island list and earns nothing for 30 epochs. A farm of 1,000 fakes pays 1,000 taxes each epoch.
